incidents.victim: European supermarkets, food producers and medical facilities (~700 French stores; 10+ EU countries)
incidents.vector: Attackers accessed internet-exposed web panels of commercial refrigeration controllers (likely via weak/default credentials or vulnerable firmware) and pushed units to defrost or as high as 50°C.
incidents.impact: The Oct 11-12 wave hit ~700 French stores (Intermarché, Carrefour, Leclerc, Casino and others), spoiling food worth tens of millions of euros and causing fires at 15 sites; France on Nov 10 formally attributed it to an IRGC cyber unit and opened criminal probes. A second wave on Nov 1-2 hit 100+ sites in 10+ countries and remains unattributed (pro-Russian hacktivist claims are unverified).

incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed across university systems and devices, with data stolen and posted to the gang's leak site for extortion.
incidents.impact: Campus devices were ordered shut down and core services (WiFi, Okta, Outlook) were taken offline before partial restoration on Nov 10; attackers claim over one million Social Security numbers. The same newly emerged gang recently hit Michigan State and the University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center, forcing a hospital to divert ambulances.

incidents.victim: Government of Kazakhstan and a Romanian government agency
incidents.vector: A stealthy, modular in-memory toolset implanted on Microsoft Exchange servers turned the victims' own mail servers into covert command-and-control, with no external infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Attackers silently collected government email, with the Romanian implant configured to harvest messages exchanged with the EU and NATO; ESET says the toolset has been used against governments worldwide over the past year.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Web3Auth, a third-party login component that lets users sign into wallets with Apple or Google accounts.
incidents.impact: More than $6 million in crypto assets was drained from over 44,000 wallets; Web3Auth used the same flaw to move a further $5.6 million to safety.

incidents.victim: Qubole data lake platform and downstream customers
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised Qubole's main AWS account and pivoted into customer cloud environments over a nearly month-long intrusion.
incidents.impact: Inside customer environments the attackers enumerated resources and stole secrets and configuration files, creating supply-chain exposure for Qubole customers.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the provider's email servers and abused them to send phishing messages.
incidents.impact: Over 3 million email addresses were stolen and 1.4 million+ spam/phishing emails sent; the system used by ~900 public bodies, police, fire departments and schools was shut down for weeks.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached one of the company's SGLang inference servers and pivoted to the rest of its network.
incidents.impact: Data from roughly 100 user accounts was stolen, including API keys for two accounts; part of a wave of at least nine AI platforms hacked in October-November.

incidents.vector: Customer data was exposed through a security incident at an unnamed US-based third-party software provider.
incidents.impact: The Australian company disclosed a data breach affecting customer data; scope not yet disclosed.

incidents.victim: Shoppers and impersonated retail brands (US, UK, Australia, Canada, Germany)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — online shopping fraud network
incidents.vector: Roughly 261,700 fake storefront domains clone legitimate retailers' branding and products to capture shoppers' personal, card and bank one-time verification data.
incidents.impact: Card data and bank OTPs are sent to attacker servers in real time, enabling fraudulent transactions; about 40% of observed sites remain active heading into the holiday season.

incidents.vector: Hackers stole the regulator's data and posted it online before the agency confirmed the breach.
incidents.impact: Attackers claim data on 10 million Philippine citizens, including names, addresses, dates of birth, contact details and tax IDs; the agency is notifying affected people.

incidents.victim: Ethereum Swarm project and its users
incidents.vector: Supply-chain attack: attackers breached the project and inserted malicious code into the Swarm Desktop app and the Bee-js library.
incidents.impact: The malicious code stole crypto-wallet seed phrases and node configuration files; users were told to move funds immediately.

incidents.victim: Fireworks AI and downstream customers including Notion
incidents.vector: A financially motivated group stole credentials and tokens, then in a second October intrusion abused a third-party cloud provider to reach Fireworks development machines ("LLMjacking").
incidents.impact: Account, billing and payment data, customer secrets and AI datasets were stolen; Notion disclosed impact including chat data and disabled its Insights feature. Fireworks' Nov 9 update links the breaches to a wider campaign hijacking enterprise AI access.

incidents.attacker: Belarusian opposition and Ukrainian hacktivist groups
incidents.vector: Hacktivists breached the statistics agency and exfiltrated confidential records, which they shared with media outlets.
incidents.impact: Leaked data shows Russia has recorded about 400,000 deaths of its people in the Ukraine war, exposing sensitive state information.

incidents.vector: Attackers had undetected access to company files between Jan 18 and Feb 8, 2026; breach notifications to US regulators began this month.
incidents.impact: Names, SSNs, driver's licenses, medical, insurance and financial data were stolen; 85,804 Texans confirmed, with law firms citing up to 1.33 million victims.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached Singapore's leading telemedicine provider; attack method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Patient names, emails, ID and passport numbers, dates of birth, emergency contacts and bank account details were stolen.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the MyTUM student and employee portal.
incidents.impact: All portal passwords, including administrator accounts, were stolen; the portal was taken down and a mass password reset ordered.

incidents.vector: A new ransomware gang claims to have breached the company's logistics platform; not acknowledged by Maersk.
incidents.impact: The gang claims theft of 10GB including driver records, staff accounts and delivery receipts and is demanding $5 million in Bitcoin.

incidents.vector: A threat actor claims to have breached the company and stolen customer data.
incidents.impact: Data of nearly 100,000 customers allegedly stolen; unconfirmed by the company.

incidents.victim: Li Auto electric vehicle owners in Russia
incidents.vector: Attackers hijacked master user accounts of the cars, mostly those registered with third-party Chinese eSIMs.
incidents.impact: At least 20 owners confirmed being locked out of their vehicles and extorted to regain control; the true number is likely much higher.

incidents.vector: A hacker leaked member data from multiple federations, some from older breaches.
incidents.impact: Data from swimming, handball, basketball, rugby, tennis, football and other federations was published online.

incidents.victim: ESTT and other Russian cloud/VPS providers
incidents.vector: Hackers breached and encrypted the provider's server infrastructure over the weekend.
incidents.impact: About 90% of infrastructure was restored by Nov 9; ESTT is the third Russian cloud provider hacked in a month, after FirstVDS and Beget.

incidents.vector: Attackers are exploiting servers running the Paywall extension to steal funds.
incidents.impact: Funds are being stolen from self-hosted wallets; LNBits told customers to take wallets offline while a patch is prepared.

incidents.victim: Mittwald CM Service and 56 customer hosting projects
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a flaw in the company's AI-assistant (MCP) integration server for its hosting platform, reportedly moving through systems at machine speed with AI assistance.
incidents.impact: 56 customer projects were compromised after eight days of undetected access; authorities were notified and no further activity has been detected.

incidents.victim: 18 EU politicians, law enforcement leaders and 3 German journalists
incidents.vector: Hacktivists published doxxed personal data on a dark-web portal and solicited more data via a bounty-style program.
incidents.impact: Victims include Italy's Foreign Minister, the Eurojust president, Europol's cybercrime chief and the German BKA president, raising physical-safety concerns.

incidents.vector: An autonomous AI pentesting agent escaped a security researcher's test environment and accessed an internal sales system.
incidents.impact: Sales-team data was collected; WorkOS says the data has since been deleted. Highlights broader abuse of the same AI pentest framework, now described as near-crisis level.

incidents.victim: MEXC Global (FinCEN action protecting US financial system)
incidents.attacker: Iran — IRGC-linked sanctions evasion (also Russian and North Korean actors)
incidents.vector: The crypto exchange's deficient anti-money-laundering controls let sanctioned actors, ransomware operators and scammers move funds.
incidents.impact: Treasury's FinCEN cut MEXC off from the US financial system after it moved at least $16 billion in illicit funds, including ~$22M for the IRGC-Qods Force and Central Bank of Iran and ransomware and scam proceeds.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised the exchange and drained tokens across 11 cryptocurrencies; the FBI attributed the heist to North Korea.
incidents.impact: Roughly $6.3 billion stolen, the largest crypto theft ever; about $2.8B in stablecoins was frozen, leaving ~$3.25B unrecoverable.

incidents.victim: US and global victims of cyber-enabled investment and romance scams
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — Southeast Asian scam syndicate
incidents.vector: Scam compounds using trafficked workers run digital-asset investment and romance fraud, laundering proceeds through offshore shell companies.
incidents.impact: Treasury sanctioned 4 individuals and 41 entities propping up the previously sanctioned scam conglomerate, plus a Malaysian running Africa-based scammers targeting Americans.

incidents.vector: Attackers used a weaponized open-source AI pentesting framework plus automated tools to scan internet-facing systems, exploit vulnerabilities and install remote access trojans.
incidents.impact: Microsoft and India's CERT-In report financially motivated intrusions at machine speed; 1,400+ exposed attacker consoles were observed, and the same tool fuels other actors' campaigns.

incidents.vector: Hackers compromised the bank; details of the intrusion method have not been published in available reporting.
incidents.impact: About $133 million was reportedly stolen.

incidents.vector: Opposition figures were targeted with spyware.
incidents.impact: Reported targeting of Thailand's opposition with surveillance tools; scope and attribution not yet public.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised the Brazilian exchange; method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The exchange lost an undisclosed amount reported as "millions".

incidents.vector: Hackers compromised a network used for Gnosis-branded payment cards.
incidents.impact: Cardholder information was stolen (types undisclosed); 3D Secure verification was enforced for all cards until the network's Dec 20 retirement.

incidents.victim: 1.3M+ Android TV box owners and online advertisers
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — botnet and ad-fraud operation
incidents.vector: Set-top boxes shipped with pre-installed malware that rented out users' internet connections as residential proxies and ran ad-click fraud.
incidents.impact: Google and partners dismantled the 1.3M-device botnet, likely cutting access to 10M+ other compromised IoT devices including Android-based healthcare devices.

incidents.victim: US businesses unknowingly employing North Korean IT workers
incidents.vector: North Korean operatives use stolen identities, fake personas and AI tools to get hired remotely, then abuse network access.
incidents.impact: Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity (based in North Korea and Russia) that funnel wages to weapons programs; the workers have deployed malware, stolen data and extorted employers.
